feedback_correct: Correct. A commit records a snapshot of every tracked file as staged at that moment, not only the lines that changed since the previous commit.

feedback_by_distractor.B: This option treats a commit as recording only the lines that changed, but a commit stores a snapshot of every tracked file as it stood when staged.
feedback_by_distractor.C: This option treats a commit as accumulating the whole project history inside itself, rather than as one point-in-time snapshot linked to its parent commit.
feedback_by_distractor.D: This option describes the working directory, including unstaged changes; a commit only ever reflects what was staged, not the full working directory.

feedback_correct: Correct. Merging integrates one branch's own work into another; whether that produces a new commit depends on whether history allows a fast-forward.

feedback_by_distractor.B: This option assumes every merge must add a new commit; a fast-forward merge only moves a branch label forward, so no merge commit is created.
feedback_by_distractor.C: This option mixes up when a conflict marker is added with when a commit is created; the two happen at different points in a merge.
feedback_by_distractor.D: This option treats the merge as finished once conflict markers in the working directory are resolved, but the merge is not complete until the resolved files are staged and committed.
